content.problemStatement:
With an input string `s` and a pattern `p`, implement regular-expression-style matching with support for `.` and `*` where:

- `.` Matches any single character.
- `*` Matches zero or more of the preceding element (the element is either a lowercase letter or `.`).

The match must cover the **entire** input string (not partial). Every `*` in `p` is guaranteed to have a valid preceding element. Output `true` if `p` matches the whole string `s`, otherwise output `false`.

Examples of semantics to keep in mind:
- `a*` can match `""`, `"a"`, `"aa"`, `"aaa"`, etc.
- `.` matches exactly one character.
- `.*` matches any sequence of characters (including the empty sequence).

Design an algorithm that runs in O of S times O of P and uses O of P space in the straightforward DP formulation (or O of P space with rolling DP).
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters (a-z).
p contains only lowercase English letters (a-z), '.' and '*'.
Every '*' has a valid preceding element.
Expected optimal time complexity: O(|s| * |p|). Expected auxiliary space: O(|s| * |p|) for full DP or O(|p|) with rolling DP.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of two strings: [s, p]. Example: ["aa","a*"]
content.outputFormat: Single line: JSON-serialized boolean: true or false
notes: The pattern must match the entire string `s` from start to end.
A `*` always modifies the immediately preceding element only.
Patterns like `a*b*c*` can match the empty string.
Be careful with indexing when checking `p[j+1]` — always check bounds first.

sampleTestCases.explanation: Pattern `a` matches exactly one 'a', but `s` has two characters; full-string match fails.
`a*` can match two 'a' characters, so the entire string is matched.
`.` matches any single character and `*` allows repetition; `.*` can match the whole string.

solution.approach: Bottom-up dynamic programming (or recursion with memoization). Build a DP table where dp[i][j] indicates whether s[i:] matches p[j:]. Handle '*' by considering zero occurrences (skip two pattern chars) or one/more occurrences (consume one char from s and stay at the same pattern position).
solution.spaceComplexity: O(|s| * |p|) for full DP; O(|p|) with rolling 1D DP

optimal.description: Use dynamic programming or recursion with memoization. Treat `*` as a modifier for the preceding element (zero or more occurrences) and `.` as a single-character wildcard. Both bottom-up DP and top-down memoized recursion run in O(|s| * |p|) time.
